newsitem.title: RUSSIA: AGROKHLEB-Russia wheat price, Kazakh supply, to rise.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB-Russia wheat price, Kazakh supply, to rise.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from SovEcon Ltd, an independent research organisation specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union.
RUSSIAN WHEAT PRICES AND KAZAKH DELIVERIES TO RUSSIA MAY RISE

MOSCOW, March 27 - On the basis of grain price dynamics in Russia, Ukraine and Kazakhstan, SovEcon expects a slow increase in Russian milling wheat prices this spring and a rise in deliveries from Kazakhstan.
Ukrainian offers have not been competitive with Kazakh or even most Russian supplies.

Russia's grain-belt Krasnodar and Stavropol regions, in the Northern Caucasus, are offering third-class milling wheat at prices ranging from 930,000 to 965,000 roubles per tonne, including loading onto rail wagons but not delivery or other charges.
But offered quantities are small and sellers are requiring pre-payment.
Due to a shortage, wheat offered on similar terms by the Rostov region, also in the Northern Caucasus, is going for 1.1-1.3 million roubles per tonne.
Rostov, usually a wheat surplus area, has even started to import milling wheat from neighbouring Stavropol.
Volgograd region, usually a wheat exporter, may also start importing Stavropol wheat.
In mid-March, the price of third-class milling wheat class delivered from the Samara region (in Povolzhsk - the Volga River area) increased from one million roubles to 1.01 million per tonne.
Third-class wheat from the Urals was offered at 950,000 roubles per tonne, but only through mid-March.
Offers of fourth class wheat from Central Chernozem (the Black Earth) region were in effect until mid-March.
Offers of domestic milling wheat are declining, with the terms of deliveries (i.e. advance payment) becoming severe.
However, increases in prices are negligible, due to the financial constraints of wheat consumers.
At the same time, prices for second-class milling wheat from Kazakhstan declined in March to $173 per tonne from $183, both both prices delivery at frontier.
In March, Kazakh third-class milling wheat was offered at $158-165 per tonne.
Third-class milling wheat from Ukraine is offered at $198 per tonne, delivery duty paid.
